recipes.name: Hamburger Vegetable Soup
ingredients_raw: 2 (1 ounce) packages dry onion soup mix

steps.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir ground beef in the hot skillet until crumbly and browned, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from heat; cover and keep warm.

Combine broth, water, frozen vegetables, tomato sauce, celery, onion, macaroni, and soup mix in a large stock pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer until macaroni is tender yet firm to the bite, about 8 minutes.
Add browned ground beef to the stock pot; mix until incorporated. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Hamburger Vegetable Soup
raw_recipe.description: This quick and easy hamburger vegetable soup recipe combines ground beef, mixed vegetables, macaroni, and tomato sauce for a satisfying 30-minute meal.

review.reviewBody: After reading most of the reviews I thought I'd share my experience in hopes that someone may be encouraged to try this truly delicious, easy and satisfying meal. First of all, try to follow the directions as they are. If you wander off the recipe you might get a stew, onion soup, or bland goulash. I followed the recipe to the "T" except for the frozen veggies; I used fresh. I must say I was a bit hesitant about using onion soup mix along with 1 onion; I feared a tummy ache all night...oh no' I slept very cozy and satisfied. I baked soft rolls to complete this dinner. My husband did prefer it a little spicier as in "hot" but my son LOVED it. Which is what many reviewers' children also say. Do not fear the onion...and by the way, this IS a soup and a very hearty one at that. Excellent recipe!

I added some extra green beans and corn and carrots chopped up as well as used beef consomme soup for flavor. I did not use 4 cups water, just 2 cups because of that. I had some leftover cooked rice I added after I turned the heat down. That added nice depth and flavor as well. Delicious!

I just made this and it is so yummy. I sauted the onions and celery before adding to the broth. I used fresh veggies instead of frozen. I also added more noodles and water since I love a heartier soup. Finally, instead of tomato paste, I added diced tomatoes with chili peppers. Added a very nice zestiness to the soup.

I follow this recipe almost exactly. I use beef broth instead of chicken and i use more of it than the water. My husband and i like our soup on the onion side so i actually add 2 lipton onion soup packets. i also add some yukon potatoes. I sauté the onion and celery in the soup pot and i brown the beef with garlic. i throw everything in the pot at the same time except the pasta. i cook that on the side and add it to the soup the last 5 minutes of simmering. we absolutely love this soup. to make it extra awesome, add some grated parm cheese to the top of your bowl and mix it in. so good.

My family loved this soup! I changed the recipe some to accommodate our taste. I like a thicker soup so I added three cans of 8 oz. tomato sauce and two cans of diced tomatoes. instead of four cups of chicken broth/ and four cups water, I used a combo of 6: 2 as I didnt want it to be too watery. I also added three bay leaves and italian seasonings to the soup. I boiled the noodles separately and added them in the end with the meat sauteed with onions and green peppers. it was so good. will do again and again

We really enjoyed this soup. I did make it in the crock pot, and cooked the macaroni separate, and added to soup just before serving. My frozen mixed vegatables came in 12 OZ packages, so I used 2 bags, which was perfect. Smelled very oniony when cooking, but did not taste overly oniony. Will definately make again!!

I, too, shied away from using all the onion soup mix. I doubled the recipe, but didn't change the amount of soup mix - and I'm glad I did. To avoid soggy noodles, I cooked the macaroni separately and served the soup over it. A simple and tasty soup - I will definitely be making it again.

So good on a cold winter day. I did mine in the crockpot. Put in the onions, celery, used 3 red potatoes cubed and one sweet potato cubed, meat, onion soup mix, vegetables, tomato sauce, 2 cans of water and 2 cans of chicken broth. It was perfect after 8 hours on low. Made about 7 quarts. Served with Sister Shubert yeast rolls!! Perfect.

I made this recipe tonight for our family and it was delish! I made a few changes because I had to feed 10 people. 2 lbs. of hamburger, i small onion chopped, 2 stalks of celery chopped, 2 packs of dry onion soup mix, 1 can of fire roasted tomatoes, 1 can of stewed tomatoes, 4 cups of chicken broth, 1 lg can of V8 juice, 1 bag of mixed frozen veg., 1 box of frozen spinach thawed, 2 medium size potatoes cut up small, and 1 tsp. garlic pepper, 1 tsp. sweet basil leaves, and noodles ( 2 hands full ) I used country style. Simmer for an hour and serve with chedder garlic bisquits. My family loved it, and certainly going to make it alot!! Thanks for the basic ingredients!! Love it!
For a low-carb version, I omitted the noodles ,I only used 3 cups of water, and only used 1 pack of the onion soup mix. I added 1 cup of frozen okra for more veggies. It was perfect.

I liked it! But I did use the suggestions like garlic powder, Italian seasoning and one package of onion soup (might try both next time)... then I added two cans of stewed tomatoes a can of past and a can of sauce, because I only had a small can of sauce. I also put 2lbs of hamburger in it and 3 cups of veggies (1 cup of each of corn, green beans and carrots). It was almost like a stew instead...
Super easy! Great when topped with Parmesean cheese!
Easy to follow. Worth the effort. Hot, hearty & filling. I will definitely make this again.

I love the simplicity of this soup recipe as written! And it just gets better the next day and the day thereafter!! On day two of leftovers, I did add a couple shakes of worcestshire sauce to the big pot. I thought a wee bit would be nice. 😀

I made this yummy soup again. This time I doubled the recipe. Like before I omitted the noodles and ground beef. I also left out the onion since I'm using the dry onion soup mix. Perfect remedy for a cold winter night
Usually I use frozen vegetables as well, also what I have in the fridge. Use up what you have, vegetables are always good together. Also, I use bouillon with this soup. It's delicious
very tasty, made as written. easy to make and everyone loved it.
